question: How much of the access-profile read/decode advantage remains for a real indexed extraction to disk, and how many archive bytes does it read?
scope: existing public dev (DEV-023 final trees); not a holdout; warm cache; one machine
archives: per class and cap: bounded-pack seed CAP FINAL_TREE once, then verify; SHA256 and size must equal research/configs/bounded-extract-reference-r0.json (DEV-023 fresh outputs)
cap_orders: round r uses frame_limits rotated left by r
profile_order: round 0 and 2: access-profile then extract-profile; round 1 and 3: extract then access
cache: archive file read once before each profile command; no global cache dropping; warm cache
execution: India vps-in1 via in-long-task, exclusive; one command at a time; measured child pinned to one CPU; timeout 1800 s per command
checks: extract and access choose the same sample paths
extract decoded bytes <= cap and >= requested per sample
extract archive bytes read <= archive size
extract output directory empty after each profile
analysis: per class / cap: extract and access median and p95, min-median-max over rounds
same-round access/extract ratio and extract whole/cap ratio
archive bytes read and decoded bytes per sample versus archive size
extract time split: index, frame read, decode, write+commit
